name: Devbox Agents
tagline: Run Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity in persistent tmux sessions and isolated git worktrees on a remote Linux devbox.
relatedBlogTitle: Managing AI Agents on a Remote Devbox
description: A VS Code extension to start, monitor, and resume autonomous AI coding agents (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Antigravity CLI) on a remote devbox over VS Code Remote - SSH. Every agent runs in its own dedicated git worktree and tmux session, continuing execution uninterrupted even when your laptop sleeps or disconnects.

features.title: One-Click Agent Worktree Provisioning
features.description: Start Claude Code, Codex, or Antigravity (agy) in an isolated git worktree (<worktreesRoot>/<repo>/<name>) on a dedicated branch (agent/<name>), inside an independent tmux session.

features.title: Uninterrupted Remote Execution
features.description: Agents execute on the remote Linux host inside tmux. They never terminate when your laptop closes, Wi-Fi drops, or the SSH connection is interrupted.

features.title: Active Session Control Plane & Explorer
features.description: Focusing a session immediately aligns your workspace: the worktree folder appears in VS Code, diffs render in the editor, and the terminal connects directly to the tmux session.

features.title: Process Inspection & Orphan Detection
features.description: Inspects running agent PIDs across the server via /proc, detecting whether they are active in tmux, running via SSH, or orphaned, with safe kill controls.

features.title: Safe Worktree Cleanup
features.description: Clean up stops tmux sessions and tears down worktrees only when there are no uncommitted or untracked changes, keeping git branches safe.

features.title: Smart Notifications & Status Hooks
features.description: Lightweight status hooks notify you immediately when an agent finishes its turn or pauses waiting for user permission or input.

features.title: Chat History & Resume
features.description: Browse past agent chat sessions by repository and worktree, and resume previous discussions directly in their original directory.

laptop: Remote - SSH (or WSL / Dev Containers / Codespaces)

agentQuickStart.title: Give this to Claude / Codex / your agent
agentQuickStart.intro: Let your coding agent set everything up. Paste this into Claude Code, Codex or another agent that can run commands on your laptop:
agentQuickStart.prompt:
Set up the VS Code extension "Devbox Agents" (royberris.devbox-agents) for me.
Follow the README: https://github.com/royberris/devbox-vscode-extension#readme

Ask me first for the SSH host of my remote dev box if you don't know it.

1. Laptop: make sure VS Code and the "Remote - SSH" extension
   (ms-vscode-remote.remote-ssh) are installed, and that `ssh <host>` works.
2. Server: install the requirements from the README section "What you install
   yourself": Linux, tmux >= 3.2, git >= 2.38, bash, and at least one agent CLI
   (Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity `agy`; ask me which). Verify the versions
   in a login shell (`ssh <host> bash -lc ...`). Use sudo only where needed and
   ask before changing system packages. Do not log in to the agents for me; tell
   me to run `claude` / `codex login` / `agy` on the server myself if needed.
3. Extension: it must be installed on the remote side ("Getting started",
   step 2). Try `code --remote ssh-remote+<host> --install-extension
   royberris.devbox-agents`; if that doesn't work, ask me to install it from the
   Extensions view in a VS Code window connected to the server.
4. Settings: follow "Getting started". Find where my repositories live on the
   server and set devboxAgents.repoRoots and devboxAgents.worktreesRoot in the
   remote machine settings (keep worktrees outside the repositories, see
   "Where to put worktrees").
5. Notifications: explain "Status hooks", then ask me whether to install them.
   If my agent config is generated by dotfiles or provisioning, add the hooks
   there instead, as described in the README.

Finish with a short summary: what you installed, the versions, the settings you
set, and anything I still have to do by hand.

quickStart: Connect VS Code to the server (e.g. Remote-SSH: Connect to Host…).
In that window, install Devbox Agents from the Extensions view (or VS Code Marketplace).
Run 'Devbox Agents: Open Settings' and verify repoRoots (default ~/repos) and worktreesRoot (default ~/worktrees).
Run 'Devbox Agents: Install Status Hooks...' once to get notifications when agents wait for input or finish.
Click '+' in the Sessions view and select Claude Code, Codex, or Antigravity.

settings.name: devboxAgents.repoRoots
settings.description: Directories containing your source repositories on the remote server.

settings.name: devboxAgents.worktreesRoot
settings.description: Base directory where isolated git worktrees are created.

settings.name: devboxAgents.branchPrefix
settings.description: Prefix for branches created per session.

settings.name: devboxAgents.focusMode
settings.description: Workspace behavior on focus (activeSessions, swapFolder, addFolder, terminalOnly).
